title: Knots, ropes and a right angle

probes.question: Which set of side lengths makes a right triangle?
True or false: in a 3-4-5 triangle, the right angle is between the sides of length 3 and 4.

image.alt: A weathered Babylonian clay tablet, Plimpton 322, covered in rows of cuneiform numerals.

panels.text: Ancient Egypt had rope stretchers, surveyors who marked land and building foundations with knotted cords pulled tight so they did not sag.
They used 3-4-5 triangles. Why that triple? Because 3 squared plus 4 squared is 9 + 16 = 25, which is 5 squared.
A triangle whose sides are a Pythagorean triple like (3, 4, 5) is a right triangle. The right angle sits between the sides of length 3 and 4.
So a loop of rope knotted into 12 equal spaces, pulled taut into 3, 4 and 5, gives a perfect corner. Modern surveyors still use the trick.
